terra.problem: Saying he is not going to joke comments on how he tells the passage. He can simply acknowledge that the moment is heavy.
Aaron being Moses’ brother and Pharaoh’s earlier refusals are facts from outside this passage, but no references are given for them.
Aaron being Moses’ brother is a fact from outside this passage and needs a reference.
Aaron being Moses’ brother is a fact from outside this passage and needs a reference.
Saying that Pharaoh is gone by midnight suggests a different Pharaoh or that he has died. The passage says neither.
The claim about Pharaoh’s responses during the plagues draws on earlier passages without a reference.
Calling the three-day journey Moses’ idea adds an origin the text does not give. The LORD instructed Moses to request it in Exodus 3:18.
The joke imagines Papa carrying a bowl on his shoulders at a run. His gold base is part of him, and he uses his mustache to carry things.
The passage does not say that nobody was turned away or that the Israelites left with more than they had when they came to Egypt.
The passage does not say that nobody had empty hands, or what anyone would have guessed a few weeks earlier.
The passage says the Israelites journeyed from Rameses to Succoth; it does not call Succoth their first stop.
The passage does not call Succoth their first stop.
Jacob is named without a brief introduction, and the reference to his dream needs the relevant verses, not just Genesis 28:19.
The passage does not call Succoth their first stop or establish everywhere the journey will take them.
Abraham is named without a brief introduction. Genesis 13:18 calls him Abram, so identifying him as Abraham also needs the verse that explicitly connects the names, Genesis 17:5.
The lunch joke brings up a meal that is not among the foods allowed for jokes.
The passage does not say dough was all they had. It also does not specify that they baked the loaves along the way.
The passage says they could not delay and had not prepared provisions. It does not say they had no time to pack anything.
The passage gives the exact duration but does not state an appointed departure day against which they could be early or late.
Aaron being Moses’ brother is a fact from outside this passage and needs a reference.
